question: Should reply-session conflict identity become a supported public `plugin-sdk/error-runtime` contract for channel plugins?
rationale: The helper is generic and removes duplicated channel logic, but publishing it commits OpenClaw to an API derived from a core session implementation detail; repository policy requires intentional ownership of that boundary.

options.title: Approve The Narrow Contract
options.body: Keep the single error-runtime predicate, require exact compatibility tests and live delivery proof, and treat its name and matching semantics as supported plugin API.

options.title: Use A Dedicated Session Subpath
options.body: Expose the behavior through a more explicitly session-owned runtime subpath so generic error-runtime does not accumulate core-specific classifications.

options.title: Keep It Internal
options.body: Do not publish the classifier and retain channel-local handling until a more stable typed conflict outcome exists.

recommendation.title: Approve The Narrow Contract
recommendation.body: Keep the single error-runtime predicate, require exact compatibility tests and live delivery proof, and treat its name and matching semantics as supported plugin API.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent work and merge history covers the guarded reply-session initialization boundary whose error identity would become public.
